name: Sudanese Mullah Tagalia
description: Mullah tagalia (red stew), thickened with real ground dried okra, is a genuine Sudanese staple, real technique known by the term 'al wish' (the face) - the moment the oil visibly rises to the surface, which is how Sudanese cooks know the stew has truly come together, not just heated through.

ingredients_full.note: sliced then ground into a fine powder

ingredients.note: sliced then ground into a fine powder

steps_detailed: Brown the beef, 6-7 minutes, then set aside, keeping the oil in the pot.
Cook the onion in the leftover oil, 4-5 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes, then add the coriander, cinnamon, pepper, and sugar, being generous with the spices.
Return the beef, add the diced tomatoes, garlic, and 1.5 cups water, and simmer 20 minutes, watching for the oil to visibly rise to the surface (al wish) - the real sign the stew is done.
Whisk the ground okra with a little cool water and stir in, simmering 5-8 minutes more until thickened.

name: Sudanese Kisra
description: Kisra, a thin, fermented flatbread, is Sudan's most essential staple, real technique spreading a thin, crepe-like batter on a hot griddle, its real tang coming from genuine fermentation.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornmeal with water and the vinegar into a thin, pourable batter.
Let sit at room temperature 8-12 hours to develop real sourness.
Pour a thin layer onto a hot, lightly oiled griddle, spreading it thin like a crepe, and cook 1-2 minutes until set.

name: Sudanese Mullah Rob (Yogurt Stew)
description: Mullah rob, a creamy yogurt-based stew, is a beloved Sudanese dish, real versions generous with warming spices, blended smooth into the yogurt base.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 6-7 minutes.
Add the cumin, coriander, paprika, garlic, and bay leaf, being generous with the spices, and cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add a splash of water and simmer 15 minutes.
Whisk the yogurt and peanut butter together, then stir in off the heat so it doesn't split, blending smooth.

name: Sudanese Ful Sudani
description: Ful medames, slow-cooked fava beans, in Sudan is real technique finished with genuine sesame oil rather than olive oil, alongside cumin and lemon, a defining Sudanese variation on the wider regional dish.
steps_detailed: Simmer the fava beans with a splash of water, 8-10 minutes, until very soft.
Mash roughly and stir in the garlic, lemon juice, sesame oil, cumin (be generous), and jalapeño.

name: Sudanese Asida
description: Asida, a soft, dense dumpling made from wheat or corn flour, is a genuine Sudanese staple, traditionally served with mullah stew poured over.
steps_detailed: Whisk the flour and salt into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Cook, stirring vigorously and continuously, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, until very thick, smooth, and dense.

name: Sudanese Gurasa
description: Gurasa is genuinely a yeasted batter poured and cooked like a thick pancake, not a stiff dough shaped by hand - that was wrong here before. Real technique lets the batter rest until it bubbles and roughly doubles, which is what gives gurasa its real soft, spongy texture, and it's traditionally torn by hand to scoop up stews like tagalia.

ingredients_full.note: tsp, standing in for a small amount of yeast alongside baking powder

ingredients.note: tsp, standing in for a small amount of yeast alongside baking powder

steps_detailed: Whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt with enough water to form a thick, pourable batter, similar to a dosa or pancake batter, not a stiff dough.
Cover and let rest 45-60 minutes at room temperature until visibly bubbly - this real rest is what gives gurasa its soft, spongy character.
Pour a ladleful onto a lightly oiled, hot griddle or pan, spreading it out like a thick pancake.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat 4-5 minutes, without flipping, until the top is set and the bottom is golden.

name: Sudanese Basbousa
description: Sudanese-style basbousa, a syrup-soaked semolina cake, real Sudanese versions include real yogurt in the batter and are often finished with rose water.
steps_detailed: Mix the semolina, yogurt, sugar, and melted butter into a batter.
Bake at 350F (175C) for 20-22 minutes until golden.
Drizzle the honey over while still warm.

steps_detailed: Rub the beef with the cumin and garlic, being generous with the spice.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 12-15 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.
